MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE
  Monday, April 4, 2022

1.  A regular meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by Mayor Hepburn at 6:32 p. m.
2.  Council Members present:  Mayor Tim Hepburn
  Mayor Pro Tem Muir Davis
  Council Member Robin Carder
  Council Member Wendy Lau
  Council Member Rick Crosby

  Absent:  None.

  Advisory personnel present:  City Manager Robert Russi
  Assistant to the City Manager JR Ranells
  City Attorney Robert L. Kress
  Assistant City Clerk Lupe Gaeta Estrella
  Finance Director Marla Pendleton

3.  Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Wendy Lau.

4.  Presentation of a Proclamation  Mayor Hepburn, on behalf of the City Council, presented a Proclamation
  Proclaiming the Month of April,  proclaiming the Month of April, 2022 as" Donate a Life" Month to Ambassador
  2022 as" Donate a Life"  Ina Strickland from the" Donate a Life" Foundation. The Proclamation
  recognizes that 100, 000 Individuals nationwide including 20, 000 in California,
  that are currently on the national organ transplant waiting list, and that on
  average, 17 people die each day while waiting for an organ, eye, tissue,
  marrow and blood donation which are life-giving acts recognized worldwide as
  expressions of compassion to those in need.

  Ambassador Ina Strickland from the" Donate a Life" Foundation thanked the
  City Council and spoke about the importance of being a donor.
 5.  Announcements of Upcoming  Sherry Best, President of the La Verne Historical Society reported on their
  Community Events  upcoming events. She stated that information on the events could be found on
  the City and La Verne Historical Society' s websites. She stated that by holding
  events they are raising funds for the restoration of the 1938 Inman
  International Truck and that they are currently accepting donations.

  George May, La Verne Library Manager reported that masks are no longer
  required at the Library and that soon they will have eight( 8) internet stations at
  the Library.

  Gilbert Ivey, a member of the Cultural Awareness and Social Inclusion ( CASI)
  Committee reported on the Committee' s mission to include everyone and
  invited residents to join.

 6.  Consent Calendar  It was moved by Davis, seconded by Lau, and unanimously carried, to accept,
  approve, or act on the Consent Calendar items.

  City Council Minutes  City Council Minutes of the adjourned and regular meetings of March
  21,  2022,  received and filed.
 City Council Minutes, Monday, April 4, 2022, Page 2,

Register of Audited Demands  Register of Audited Demands in the amount of$ 1, 741, 063. 52 dated March
  3, 2022; and in the amount of $ 885,288.45  dated March 10, 2022.
  Approved as recommended by Finance Director Pendleton.

  Staff recommended approval and passage of the following Resolutions:

Public Hearing  STATE OF CALIFORNIA, AND SETTING A TIME AND PLACE FOR PUBLIC
  HEARING THEREON - The property owner of 1941 N. White Avenue has
  requested that the City vacate a public utility easement located at 1941 N.
  White Avenue. The subject utility easement does not serve any known utilities.
  Setting a public hearing and providing noticing will initiate the easement
  vacation process.

  City Engineer Howing recommended that the City Council approve Resolution
  No. 22- 15, declaring its intention to initiate the procedures for the vacation of
  the public utility easements located at 1941 N. White Avenue; setting the
  public hearing for Monday, May 2, 2022 at 6: 30 p. m. and to direct the City
  Clerk to conduct noticing of the public hearing pursuant to Streets and
  Highways Code Division 9, Part 3. Approved as recommended.

Mid- Year Budget Update Fiscal  Finance Director Pendleton gave an update on the Mid- Year Budget for Fiscal
Year 2021- 22  Year 2021- 22. She reported that a recommendation to decrease the 2021- 22
  amended General Fund Appropriation Budget by$ 101, 816 from $40, 920, 192
  to$ 40,818, 376 and an increase to the anticipated revenue from $ 38, 808,915
  to $ 45,464,837 is being proposed. The net impact of the proposed budget
  adjustments will result in an anticipated increase of$ 4,646,461 to the General
  Fund reserves (fund balance) at the end of the fiscal year which $ 4, 000,000 is
  recommended to be transferred to fund the Section 115 pension trust. Overall,
  revised year-end estimates now reflect a General Fund surplus of$ 646,461.

  Finance Director Pendleton continued to report that the Mid- Year Budget
  Report includes the recommended appropriation budget for use of the
  7, 648.860 American Rescue Plan Act( ARPA) allocation, separating the
  emergency firefighting budget from the General Fund into its own fund,
  California Fire Assistance Agreement( CFAA) Reimbursable, Fund 110, and
  increasing the Measure LV sales tax revenue by$ 1, 100, 000.
  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this matter.

  There were public comments at the meeting. ( To hear what was said during
  public comment, please visit the City' s website to view the archived Council
  meeting.)

  City Manager Russi responded to the questions asked during public comment.
  The City Council was pleased with the excellent financial health of the City's
  Budget and they thanked staff for their continued excellent work in managing
  Verne.
  the budget effectively. They urged residents to continue to shop La

  It was moved by Davis, seconded by Carder, and unanimously carried to
  approve the proposed budget adjustments and Section 115 trust funding as
  presented in the Mid- Year Budget Update Fiscal Year 2021- 22.

7.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other place on the agenda.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment.

  There were public comments at the meeting. ( To hear what was said during
  public comment, please visit the City' s website to view the archived Council
  meeting.)

  City Manager Russi and City Attorney Kress responded to the questions asked
  during public comment.

8.  Council Comments  Council Member Carder reported that she attended the La Verne Fire Station
  No. 3 Reopening Ceremony and the Badge Pinning Ceremony for Police Chief
  Flores. She stated that both events were very nice.

  Council Member Crosby had no comments.

  Council Member Lau reported she also attended the La Verne Fire Station No.
  3 Reopening Ceremony and the Badge Pinning Ceremony for Police Chief
  Flores. She stated that both events were wonderful. She spoke about how
  fitting the Proclamation proclaiming the month of April as" Women' s History
  Month" and holding a badge pinning for the first female police chief. She urged
  residents to mark on your driver' s license to be donor. In addition, she
  reported that the University of La Verne is hosting a blood drive in April; and
  the University will be holding a picnic and a baseball double header honoring
  former ULV Coach Ben Hines on April 23, 2022. She finished by asking
  everyone to stay safe and to be kind to each other.

  Mayor Pro Tem Davis stated that the Reopening Ceremony for La Verne Fire
  Station No. 3 was wonderful and he thanked Captain Moore for the tour of the
  station. He stated that Southern California Edison offers solar energy
  programs. He stated that he too, attended the Badge Pinning Ceremony for
  Police Chief Flores which was very nice. He stated that with a winning Water
  Polo Team, it is necessary to repair the Las Flores swimming pool. He also
  reported on the Public Banking Association meeting, the Pomona Valley
  Transportation Authority, the La Verne/San Dimas Educational Foundation
  annual Ed Jones Memorial Golf Tournament, tribute event for former ULV
  Coach Ben Hines on April 23, 2022 and the Cultural Awareness and Social
  Inclusion ( CASI) Committee.

  Mayor Hepburn stated that he too, attended the La Verne Fire Station No. 3
  Reopening Ceremony and the Badge Pinning Ceremony for Police Chief
  Flores. He thanked the La Verne Police staff, Community Services Manager
  Duran for hosting an incredible badge pinning ceremony. He was pleased with
  Measure LV sales tax and urged residents to continue to shop La Verne and
  keep the money in La Verne. He stated he attended a" Victims of Crime"
  event.  He stated it was a memorable event and it was for a good cause.

  and City Attorney.

  Employee Organization( s):  La Verne City Employees Association,
  La Verne Police Officers' Association,
  La Verne Firefighters' Association, La Verne
  Police Middle Management Association and
  all unrepresented employees

10.  Adjournment at 8: 30 p. m., to Monday, April 18, 2022 at 6: 00 p. m. for presentation of Pride of La Verne
  Certificates to La Verne Police Retired Senior Volunteer Patrol ( RSVP) Members; Life Saving Awards to
  La Verne Police Officers and for a Fire Marshal Badge pinning ceremony.
